what: Round dish-photo-like cells sit on an arc where only the center cell is lowest and cells rise 60·150·270px toward each side. When the embla carousel (loop · center aligned · duration 20) turns one cell every 4 seconds, each cell rises or falls to its new height in .6s cubic-bezier(.33,1,.68,1). Drag to swipe, and the prev/next buttons also advance it. Pressing a button keeps autoplay going (it pauses when focus enters). It runs only while 20% of the panel is visible.

options.lift: Heights (px) that cells 1, 2, 3… away from the center rise, comma-separated. Default 60,150,270 — cells farther than the list are 0 (original position4 as is). Phone original is 89,150,270
options.duration: embla slide duration (physics units, not ms), default 20
options.view: Visible ratio at which auto-advance runs, default .2
options.--fx-size: Cell width (including gap), default 314px — if smaller than 20% of the panel width, use 20%
options.--fx-room: Top margin the cell rises into, default 270px
options.--fx-ease: Up-and-down curve, default cubic-bezier(.33,1,.68,1) — the brand type uses cubic-bezier(.83,0,.17,1) with --fx-dur: 1.75s · lift: 20,59,59,59
options.[data-fx-part=slide]: Cell — the [data-fx-part inside=lift] moves up and down (whole cell if absent)

from.where: index.js .arc — original .menu_slider: embla { duration 20, loop, align center } + ClassNames + Autoplay(delay 4000, stopOnInteraction false, stopOnFocusIn true), position±n classes on each select → .embla__slide_inner translateY -60/-150/-270 (phone ±1 is -89) · transition .6s cubic-bezier(.33,1,.68,1) · IntersectionObserver .2

index.js .mv__product · .mv__bubbles — the original Splide (loop · focus center · speed 1750 · cubic-bezier(.83,0,.17,1) · auto-advance every 4s) with is-active/prev/next-logical classes also attached to the clones, giving 0 at the center, -6% on either side and -18% for the rest (-24% for the photo bubbles), over 1.75s on the same curve. The slider library is Splide, so the feel differs from this part (embla) — to reproduce only the numbers, convert the lift into a ratio of the slide height

note: Since embla is used, embla handles dragging — it only grabs horizontal drags (touch-action: pan-y), and pushing vertically scrolls the page
